gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in the maker's own words, that the Duex Float stands on its own fold-out base with the laptop placed in front of it and that the magnets are optional. The lid and hinge do not carry its 2.9 lb. That one fact undoes both the hinge-strain warning ChatGPT repeated from Fstoppers and its 'best suited to 15–16-inch laptops' limit.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Fstoppers guide, the cited Macworld review (Simon Jary) and our own current page. Fstoppers says the Float 2 Pro mounts 'to the back of the lid with four magnets' and that 'hanging that off the back of a laptop lid stresses the hinge on thinner machines'. ChatGPT repeated this as '2.9 lb is substantial for a laptop-mounted accessory.' Macworld says the magnets keep 'the MacBook and Float as one piece' and calls the kickstand 'reasonably stable', but never says what carries the weight. Our page says 'magnets on the lid's back plus a kickstand', which is just as unclear. Macworld already has the power-side mechanism (7.5 W Limited Power Mode, brightness capped at 80%, 15 W PD charger for full brightness), so that finding is not new. Mighty Gadget (a result, but uncited) says the 2 Pro 'can free-stand' on a 'triangular base'. That keeps the weight finding from scoring 3.
decides: This confirms the Duex Float 2 Pro as the pick and widens who it suits. Its own base carries the weight, so a thin lid or a 13–14-inch laptop is not ruled out by hinge load. Mobile Pixels' Duex Float FAQ answers 'Will the Duex Float work with 12.5'', 13.3'' or 14.1'' laptops?' with 'Yes'. The real conditions it has to meet are: (1) a USB-C port with DP Alt Mode for the single-cable setup, otherwise mini-HDMI plus a separate power cable; (2) running from the laptop alone caps brightness (80% in Limited Power Mode per Macworld) until a 15 W+ PD charger is added; (3) it can't be used with a laptop stand, because the Float would sit lower than the raised laptop. ChatGPT pointed small-laptop owners to the Xebec Snap with Stack-Up Mount (about $708), which mounts on a lid bracket, so the weight logic actually points the other way.

findings.label: How it is supported / laptop size fit (maker FAQ)
findings.value: "It stands up by itself, simply place your laptop in front of it and you are ready to go." Magnets: "(Attach the Duex Float to the laptop via magnets is optional)". Answer to the 12.5/13.3/14.1-inch question: "Yes, Duex Float will work with any sized laptops."
findings.note: This FAQ page is for the original Duex Float. The Float 2 Pro product page returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I could not get the same statement in the maker's words for the 2 Pro.

findings.label: Free-standing base (named reviewer)
findings.value: Mighty Gadget (James Smythe): "the Duex Float 2 Pro can free-stand"; kickstand "forms a proper triangular base rather than a thin prop"; "It is not going anywhere on a desk, even at a fairly upright viewing angle." On magnets: "You can still attach magnets for a secure fit, but I don't really see the point."
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro Review - Mighty Gadget

findings.label: USB-C video requirement (maker installation page)
findings.value: Single USB-C cable only "For laptop has USB-C port with DP ALT mode"; USB-C plus HDMI "For laptop has USB-C port without DP ALT mode"; USB-C with a USB-A adapter plus HDMI "For laptop has only USB-A and HDMI port."
findings.note: Maker's own wording. A laptop USB-C port without DisplayPort Alt Mode will not show video over one cable.

findings.label: Brightness when powered by the laptop (maker FAQ)
findings.value: 250 nits max when powered directly from a computer, up to 300 nits with proper external power; power consumption "Max at 7W"
findings.note: Original Float. 250/300 = about 83% of full brightness when running off the laptop.

findings.label: Limited Power Mode on laptop power (named reviewer)
findings.value: Macworld (Simon Jary): "The screen will draw from 7.5W of power from the MacBook in the Limited Power Mode that caps brightness at 80%." Full brightness needs "a PD-compliant USB-C charger rated at 15W or higher."
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: This is already on a cited rival page, so it does not count toward standout.

findings.label: Laptop stand conflict (named reviewer)
findings.value: Macworld (Simon Jary): "If you use a laptop stand, this will have to be discarded when using the Float…" because the Float stays lower than a raised laptop.
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: Follows from the free-standing design: the Float's base sits on the desk.
